class.name: DriverServer
class.brief_description: The AI drivers, by the person's handle.
class.description: The drivers are [PersonServer] persons declared drivers of a named [DriverImplementation]. A driver takes the orders a scenario gives ([method driver_send_command]) and, through its implementation, what they mean; it drives the vehicle it sits in ([VehicleServer]) as a player does, through the cab, while it sits there in the driver's role. A player at the controls needs no driver. The implementations are registered by name ([method implementation_register]), as [VehicleServer]'s are: whoever declares a driver (a scenery's trainset) names what it thinks with, and knows nothing of the class. A driver of a name nobody registered yet thinks with nothing - its orders are lost - until the implementation is registered, so it is registered before the drivers get their orders. A driver acts in moments, as the original's does after its reaction time ([code]TController::ReactionTime[/code], [code]Driver.cpp:150-158[/code]): its implementation asks for the next one ([method driver_schedule_update]) and is called when it comes. The time is [SimulationServer]'s simulation time, which the physics and the events read too.

method.name: driver_attach_implementation
method.description: The person [param driver] becomes a driver thinking with the implementation registered as [param implementation] ([method implementation_register]), as soon as there is one; an empty name makes it none.

method.name: driver_get_implementation
method.description: What [param driver] thinks with; null while nothing is registered under its name.

method.name: driver_get_state
method.description: What the driver keeps, from its implementation ([method DriverImplementation._get_state]); empty without an implementation.

method.name: driver_get_timetable_state
method.description: The driver's timetable and its progress, from its implementation ([method DriverImplementation._get_timetable_state]); empty without an implementation.

method.name: driver_report_order_changed
method.description: Called by the driver's implementation when the driver takes up another order; emits [signal driver_order_changed].

method.name: driver_report_timetable_changed
method.description: Called by the driver's implementation when its timetable, or how far it got through it, has changed; emits [signal driver_timetable_changed].

method.name: driver_schedule_update
method.description: The implementation of [param driver] is updated in [param seconds] of simulated time; a later call replaces the one pending.

method.name: driver_send_command
method.description: An order for [param driver] - a scenario's [param command] with its two values, and the [param position] of what sent it.

method.name: implementation_register
method.description: [param implementation] thinks for the drivers declared with [param name], from now on those declared before it as well; a name registered again is thought with by the new one.

method.name: implementation_unregister
method.description: The drivers declared with [param name] think with nothing until it is registered again.

method.name: vehicle_get_driver
method.description: The driver aboard [param vehicle], in whatever role (the original's [code]Mechanik[/code]); an empty RID for none.

method.name: vehicle_get_seconds_until_departure
method.description: The seconds from [param hours] (the time of day) to the departure of the vehicle's train ([method DriverImplementation._get_seconds_until_departure]): by the timetable of its own driver, else of the first driver of its trainset with one ([code]Mechanik[/code], else [code]ctOwner[/code], [code]Event.cpp:2431-2435[/code]); 0 for a train without a timetable.

method.name: vehicle_is_control_active
method.description: Whether the driver of [param vehicle] sits at its controls ([code]AIControllFlag[/code]) - not while it rides along in a cab a player drives from; it still takes its orders then, but touches no control. [code]false[/code] for a vehicle without a driver.

signal.name: driver_attached
signal.description: The person is a driver now: it was given its first implementation ([method driver_attach_implementation]).

signal.name: driver_freed
signal.description: The person is no driver anymore: its implementation was taken ([method driver_attach_implementation] with null), or the person was freed (PersonServer).

signal.name: driver_order_changed
signal.description: The driver took up another order.

signal.name: driver_timetable_changed
signal.description: The driver's timetable, or how far it got through it, has changed.
